pass_a_gloss: What the prophet is commanded to say by God, he owes to be worthy of God; but it appears that it is not worthy of God, as we remain upon the letter, so as to say that someone else hearing the letter: this is foolishness, these letters. But this will say the psychic person: 'For the psychic person does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him.' See then the word what it says. 'And you will say to this people: Thus says the Lord God of Israel' — what the Lord God of Israel says, let it be worthy of the Lord of Israel — 'Every vessel shall be filled with wine. And it will be, if they say to you: Not knowing, we shall not know that every vessel shall be filled with wine'; and those answering, if standing upon the word, say these things, claiming to have known that 'Every vessel shall be filled with wine', they lie. For not 'Every vessel shall be filled with wine.' For there are vessels filled with oil or other liquid, and some therefore lie; for not 'Mᾶς vessel shall be filled with wine.' And the people answer saying: 'Not knowing, we shall not know that every vessel shall be filled with wine'; which, as far as possible, our narrative will produce such. If we know the differences of wines and what is said about them, and accordingly we shall observe the vessels, that it is true that every vessel shall be filled with wine. For if someone is good, let us call him thus, in vessels, a vessel shall be filled with wine according to his goodness. But if he is, as in comparison of vessels and judgment concerning them, wicked, and he himself according to his wickedness shall be filled with wicked wine. How then is it from the Scripture to take concerning the different wines? Concerning the inferior ones, it is written thus: 'For from the vineyard of Sodom is their vine, and their tendril from Gomorrah.' Their grape is a grape of bitterness, their cluster is bitterness to them; the wrath of dragons is their wine, and the wrath of shields is incurable. But concerning the better ones: 'Your cup which makes drunk as the strongest,' and wisdom calls upon its own crater, saying: 'Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine which I have mixed for you.' Therefore there is wine from Sodom, and there is wine, which wisdom mixes. And again: 'A vineyard became to the beloved in the horn in a place of drinking,' planted by God, the vine called Sorek, being choice and wonderful. And there is also a vine of the Egyptians, which God strikes according to what is written: 'God struck their vine with hail, and their sycamores with frost.'

pass_b_english: What the prophet is commanded by God to say ought to be worthy of God. Yet if we remain on the letter it does not appear worthy of God, so that someone hearing the letter might say: these letters are folly. But a psychic person will say this; for 'the psychic person does not receive the things of the Spirit of God; for they are folly to him.' (1 Corinthians 2:14)

Look then at what the wording says. 'And you shall say to this people: Thus says the Lord the God of Israel'—what 'the Lord the God of Israel' says, let it be worthy of the Lord of Israel—'Every wineskin will be filled with wine. And if they say to you, “Shall we not know, knowing, that every wineskin will be filled with wine?” (Deuteronomy 32:32)' And those who answer, if they say these things standing on the bare wording, claim to know that 'every wineskin will be filled with wine,' and they lie. For not every wineskin will be filled with wine. There are wineskins filled with oil or with some other liquid substance. So some lie; for not every wineskin will be filled with wine. And the people answers saying: 'Shall we not know, knowing, that every wineskin will be filled with wine?'—words that will receive an interpretation of this kind, as far as we can.

If we know the differences among wines and what is said about them, and accordingly look at the wineskins, we will see that it is true that every wineskin will be filled with wine. For whether someone is good—let us name him so among wineskins, a wineskin—he will be filled with wine according to his own goodness. Or whether he is, by comparison of wineskins and the judgment about them, wicked, he too according to his wickedness will be filled with wicked wine. How then can we take from Scripture the different wines? About the worse ones it is written like this: 'For their vine is from the vine of Sodom, and their shoot from Gomorrah.

Their grape is a grape of gall; a cluster of bitterness to them; their wine is the rage of dragons, and the incurable rage of asps.' And about the better ones: 'Your cup that makes drunk is as the strongest,' (Psalm 78:47 or Isa 28:2) and Wisdom calls to her own mixing-bowl saying: 'Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine I have mixed for you.' (Psalm 23:5 (LXX)) So there is wine from Sodom, and there is wine that Wisdom mixes. And again: 'A vineyard came to be for the beloved on a horn in a rich place,' planted by God, the vine called Sorek—choice and marvelous. And there is also a vine of the Egyptians, which God strikes according to what is written: that 'God struck their vine with hail, and their mulberry trees with frost.'
